changes.before: If the producer sends [2, 3, 4], what changes?
changes.after: A queue passes items in order. A bounded queue limits how many can wait inside it at once.

before: SizedQueue.new(1) creates a synchronized queue holding at most one waiting item. push blocks while full, pop blocks while empty, and the queue coordinates the handoff without guessing worker timing.

The single producer closes this queue after pushing all values. pop returns nil once the closed queue is empty, so nil is reserved here as end-of-stream and never sent as data. The assignment in while stores each popped item and tests its truthiness; false would also stop this loop, so the protocol sends only integers. The consumer drains before joining the producer; joining first could deadlock if the producer is blocked on a full buffer.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
queue = SizedQueue.new(1)
producer = Thread.new do
  [2, 3].each { |n| queue.push(n) }
  queue.close
end
sum = 0
while (item = queue.pop)
  sum += item
end
producer.join
puts sum

```
Expected output or behavior: 5. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

The next push may have to wait for the reader to take the current item.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.
```ruby
queue = SizedQueue.new(1)
producer = Thread.new do
  [2, 3].each { |n| queue.push(n) }
  queue.close
end
sum = 0
while (item = queue.pop)
  sum += item
end
producer.join
puts sum
```
The output is `5`. The reader adds two and three. It finishes after the producer closes the queue and the items are gone.

before.question: If the producer sends [2, 3, 4], what changes?
choices: The program must use sleep to avoid deadlock.
Only the first item survives the capacity-one limit.
The consumer drains all three and prints 9.
before.explanation: Capacity limits buffered items, not the total stream; synchronized consumption makes room until closure signals completion.

after.question: If the producer sends two, three and four, what sum prints?
after.explanation: The reader takes all three, even though only one can wait in the queue at a time.
